summary: Cleanup routine that first calls PhysicsObjectListManager (0x004B4E10), then frees four linked lists of physics/collision nodes and zeroes their 4-dword head slots. Each node carries a next pointer at +4 and a type/active byte at +8; nodes with a non-zero type byte also free the buffer pointer at the node base (+0) via FreeWrapper_7bcf, and every node struct is freed. The four 16-byte slots are zeroed across the loop, spanning byte offsets 0x70-0xAC. Returns 0. Called by SpriteOverlayListCleanup (0x004B6130).

local_names.v2: walking pointer to the current 4-dword list slot (starts at this + 44)
local_names.v3: current node pointer, also the next pointer chain
local_names.v4: node struct viewed as an LPVOID buffer holder
local_names.v5: flag: node type byte at +8 is zero

operations.description: PhysicsObjectListManager (0x004B4E10) invoked first to manage/pre-process the physics object list
Set up the walk: v2 = this + 44 (dword index 44, byte +0xB0) and outer counter v7 = 4
Four iterations total; each iteration reads the list head at *(v2 - 4), advances v2 by 16 bytes, and after the inner walk zeroes the 4-dword slot now at v2 (v2[0]..v2[3])
Inner walk: while the node pointer v3 is non-null, read the type byte at node +8 into v5 and the next pointer at node +4, and advance v3 to that next node
If the node type byte at +8 is non-zero (v5 false), the buffer at the node base (+0) is freed before the node itself
FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF) invoked to free the node's buffer when the type byte is non-zero, and always to free the node struct itself
After each inner walk the 4-dword head slot (v2[0], v2[1], v2[2], v2[3]) is zeroed
Outer loop decrements v7 from 4 and repeats until v7 equals 1, giving exactly four slot cleanups; the four zeroed slots span byte offsets 0x70-0xAC
Returns 0 once all four lists are processed
Called by SpriteOverlayListCleanup (0x004B6130) as part of overlay/sprite list teardown

unresolved: The packet fact table reports this-fields at +0xB0/+0xB4/+0xB8/+0xBC, but the decompiled pointer arithmetic (v2 = this + 44, then v2 -= 4 before zeroing v2[0..3]) places the four zeroed 16-byte slots in the +0x70 to +0xAC range; the +0xB0-0xBC group is never written by this function as decompiled, so the fact-table offsets remain unmatched

Node layout semantics (+4 next, +8 type/active byte, base buffer pointer) are inferred from the decompile; the exact meaning of the type byte and the four list roles (head/tail/next pointers) is not named by this function
The intermediate zeroing order walks the four slots in descending byte order (highest list slot first, lowest last); whether this ordering is meaningful is not established
